trickyParts: The gate is on what the block held at selection, not on what it holds now. A block that held the words once is the same passage however its sentence was rewritten, which is the case the issue was filed for; a block that held them twice and now holds one may be holding the reading the reader never selected. Only the remembered count tells those apart, and neither the current document nor the tracked range can.

The refusal reasons now say four different things, and each is true of its own case alone: the words read nowhere ('gone'); they read somewhere but not in the reader's block ('unplaceable'); they read in the reader's block but nothing there says which reading was theirs ('unsurrounded'); a suggestion's text cannot carry the mark ('unmarkable').
